chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who comes to the prayer but does not find a place in the row; should he stand alone until he finishes his prayer? He said, 'Yes, there is no harm; he should stand in line with the Imam.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person arrives late to congregational prayer and cannot fit into the existing row?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of latecomers joining the prayer row, permitting them to stand individually aligned with the Imam rather than forming a separate, disconnected row. This ruling emphasizes the spiritual and structural integrity of the congregation (jama'ah) by ensuring the latecomer remains physically and ritually connected to the leader, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maintaining communal unity even in minor jurisprudential details.
